annotations.derivable_answer: GeoCache adapts reverse reprojection caching by transporting a first difference in x0 across views of the same object inside a denoising trajectory through geometric correspondence, integrating it into the target pixel's retained value and periodically refreshing the result.

supporting_quotations.quote:
Reverse reprojection
caching (Nehab et al. 2007) provides a closer computational
pattern by transporting a per-pixel quantity through geometric correspondence, integrating it into the target pixel’s retained value, and periodically refreshing the result. GeoCache applies these operations inside a denoising trajectory
and transports a first difference inx0 across views of the
same object.

annotations.rationale: Passage 2 explicitly describes how GeoCache borrows from reverse reprojection caching by transporting the first difference in x0 across views via geometric correspondence during denoising.

annotations.derivable_answer: V-JEPA adapts joint-embedding architectures to video by predicting representations of masked spatiotemporal regions from visible spatiotemporal context using an EMA target encoder. Unlike MAE/V-MAE which reconstruct low-level pixel/texture details, V-JEPA predicts learned representations.

supporting_quotations.quote:
Because these targets are learned
representations, I-JEPA and V-JEPA use an EMA target encoder to stabilize
training[2,5].Themodelisthereforenotrequiredtoreconstructlow-level texture
or color details. V-JEPA extends the same idea to video by predicting representations of masked spatiotemporal regions from visible spatiotemporal context [5]. This places I-JEPA/V-JEPA close to MAE/V-MAE in masking structure, while
separating them by the prediction target.

annotations.rationale: Passage 2 explains V-JEPA's video extension and contrasts its learned representation target against pixel-level reconstruction in MAE/V-MAE.

annotations.derivable_answer: The evaluation framework presents ECR-R items to models individually within a fixed option set, computing mean anxiety and avoidance scores to map models onto a two-dimensional attachment space. ECBench was introduced to complement ECR-R because while ECR-R characterizes attachment tendencies, it lacks realistic interpersonal interaction contexts.

supporting_quotations.quote:
For model evaluation, we present the ECR-R
items to each model individually and require responses within a ﬁxed set of options. We then
compute the mean scores for anxiety and avoidance and map them onto a two-dimensional attachment space.

The ECR-R characterize the attachment tendencies of LLMs, but lacks realistic interpersonal interaction contexts. We therefore introduce a dialogue benchmark called ECBench for evaluating
emotional companionship capabilities in realistic
interaction scenarios.

annotations.rationale: Passage 2 explains the ECR-R administration and 2D mapping procedure, and Passage 3 explains the motivation for developing ECBench.
